{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABiAzSJw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhLYiAc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 83, "title": "Add an optional WebGL2 Retro CRT display effect and enable it by default", "body": "## Problem

The browser emulator currently presents the Rust/Wasm RGBA framebuffer using Canvas 2D and nearest-neighbor scaling. This is useful for inspecting exact pixels, but lacks the subtle scanlines, mask and softness associated with the CRT televisions and monitors commonly used with MSX computers.

The same repository owner has implemented a restrained **Retro CRT** display mode in wonderswan-rust. A similar presentation-only option would make MSX games and BASIC feel more like the original experience, while retaining the exact unfiltered output for users who prefer it.

## Expected outcome

Add a **Display** selector with two choices:

- **Retro CRT** — the default on fresh visits when WebGL2 is usable. Apply a lightweight GPU shader with subtle horizontal scanlines, a fine CRT-style mask and mild pixel softness. Keep BASIC text, game graphics and color distinctions legible.
- **Clean** — retain the existing unfiltered, nearest-neighbor Canvas 2D presentation.

Switch modes immediately without resetting or changing the emulated machine, including when paused. Remember an explicit selection locally across visits. When WebGL2 cannot initialize, fails to draw or loses its context, automatically present the playable Clean display with a nonblocking explanation. Recover the requested mode when possible.

This is an aesthetic presentation effect, not measured CRT calibration or a change to VDP/CPU accuracy. Keep the implementation small: no mandatory curvature, bloom, flicker, frame-history persistence, new graphics framework or external shader download.

## Context and reproduction

- Baseline main revision: `e9cefc70d5fc4e7e3ce274edafc8706a68804d77`.
- [wonderswan-rust display implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/bb6f672a1ec40dd688d01a1f6b312b28ad8e7359/web/src/display.ts) and [README](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/bb6f672a1ec40dd688d01a1f6b312b28ad8e7359/README.md): WebGL2 Retro CRT, restrained mask/scanlines/softness, Clean fallback, persisted preference, bounded rendering resolution and no CRT frame-history pass. Use these as a behavioral/design reference. No explicit repository license was found during drafting; independently implement the shader and integration unless permission to reuse code is established. Preserve applicable notices and document provenance.
- Unlike WonderSwan's fixed 224×144 image, MSX has changing native dimensions. The current VDP exposes 256/512-pixel widths, 192/212 active lines and doubled interlaced heights (384/424). Obtain dimensions from the actual Wasm framebuffer, not a fixed 256×192 or 224×144 assumption.
- In `web/app.js`, `render()` obtains `msx_width()`, `msx_height()` and `msx_pixels()` and draws via `screen.getContext('2d')` / `putImageData`. `web/index.html` contains the focusable `#screen`; `web/style.css` establishes the 4:3 display layout and fullscreen behavior. Existing tests inspect exact Canvas pixels, so retain an unfiltered source/presentation path for independent hardware assertions. A separate GPU presentation canvas is a reasonable approach; do not rely on acquiring 2D and WebGL2 contexts from the same canvas.
- Reproduction: open https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/, run BASIC or load a demo cartridge; the image is currently unfiltered and no CRT/Clean selector is available.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement an independently authored WebGL2 CRT shader, taking the existing RGBA framebuffer as its source. Use subtle scanline modulation, mask and mild neighbor sampling/softness, with scale-aware reduction of fine detail at small output sizes to avoid aliasing/moiré. Preserve black, orientation, palette distinctions and readable text. Keep the raw framebuffer and emulation state unchanged.
- [ ] Expose a concise, accessible Display selector with Retro CRT and Clean. A fresh browser session without an explicit preference requests Retro CRT; when supported, the first usable display uses that effect. Selecting either mode updates the visible image immediately, including when paused, without running extra emulated frames or resetting BASIC, cartridge, disk, tape, audio or input state. Persist explicit preference with a project-specific local key separate from SRAM and other saves; unavailable/corrupt storage must not prevent play.
- [ ] Correctly handle all actual framebuffer sizes and changes between MSX1/MSX2, SCREEN modes, 192/212 lines and interlaced 384/424-line output. Update texture sizes, uniforms and presentation coordinates when needed; preserve the existing 4:3 display footprint, correct aspect/orientation, responsive layout and fullscreen behavior, including resize while paused. Do not hard-code WonderSwan dimensions or treat doubled interlace lines as ordinary fixed-height progressive input.
- [ ] Keep Clean pixel-exact with current behavior. WebGL2 initialization, shader compilation/linking, rendering/resource failure and context loss must fall back to usable Clean without blocking startup or game execution. Restore the requested effect on successful context restoration; keep UI status consistent with the actually active renderer. Preserve focus, keyboard/paste and joystick input on both displays, without duplicate focus targets or invisible input interception.
- [ ] Keep GPU resource allocation bounded and reuse textures/programs across frames. Size GPU output according to actual display size/device pixel ratio with a documented sensible cap; upload/present only the latest needed frame, without extra RAF loops, GPU readback in the normal rendering path, or a CRT history pass. Switching/resizing/paused redraws must not step CPU/audio. Measure a representative real-Wasm gameplay workload with Clean versus CRT on the same browser/environment; record frame throughput and audio continuity and investigate any material regression. No subjective listening or physical GPU/CRT hardware is required.
- [ ] Add focused automated browser tests of actual composited output, not just selector values: verify a known flat/edge pattern has CRT scanline/mask modulation and subtle softness, Clean preserves exact source pixels, both modes render with correct orientation/geometry, switching preserves running and paused state, and the setting survives reload. Cover representative MSX1/MSX2 modes including a 512-wide and interlaced mode, resize/fullscreen, input, WebGL2 unavailable/failed shader/context loss and recovery, and storage failure. Verify the deployed-path build locally at both `/` and `/msx-rust/` with representative cases rather than duplicating the full matrix. Use real WebGL rendering in automated Chromium (software WebGL where necessary), not a mocked shader-success flag alone.
- [ ] Preserve the existing meaningful hardware pixel assertions by targeting the raw framebuffer/Clean path where exact values are intended. Add independent visible CRT checks so an unfiltered hidden canvas cannot falsely satisfy the new feature tests. Preserve the current MSX2-first startup, BASIC, C-BIOS, cartridge mappers/SRAM, disk/tape, sound and demo workflows. Follow the repository's test/CI performance principles: focused tests at the lightest appropriate layer, no unnecessary Cartesian-product expansion, no unrelated CI changes.
- [ ] Update README and help text for the two display modes, default/fallback, local preference, performance considerations and aesthetic limitations. Include any new static shader/module assets in the existing distribution inventory and relative-path validation. Keep deployment self-contained and preserve licenses.
- [ ] Run the configured applicable checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test`, and `git diff --check`. Report actual results, test scope, timing and limitations. Follow the existing English Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → revision → merge/close lifecycle. All required pre-merge acceptance must be AI-verifiable.

## Optional validation

The owner may compare the CRT appearance of BASIC text and legally available games with a physical CRT or the WonderSwan Retro CRT mode, on desktop/mobile/fullscreen. Subjective preference and physical monitor checks are not pre-merge gates. Further stylistic presets or stronger CRT effects can be considered separately if desired.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] After successful merge and Pages deployment, verify the published https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ build in a fresh WebGL2-capable browser session: actual default CRT output on MSX2 BASIC, live Clean/CRT switching without a reset, and a representative demo's visible output. Record deployed revision, Actions run, browser environment and observed results. Close this implemented Issue on merge; a pending post-merge check is not a reason to withhold approval or reopen it. Record any actual deployed-site defect in a linked follow-up Issue after checking for duplicates, in accordance with the current development lifecycle.
